newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WORLD CHEMICALS TRADE RISES 25 PCT IN 1995 - UN.
newsitem.headline: WORLD CHEMICALS TRADE RISES 25 PCT IN 1995 - UN.

text.p: World trade in chemicals and chemical products reached some $450 billion in 1995, nearly a 25 per cent rise on the year before, a new United Nations report said on Tuesday.
The total value of chemical trade in 1994 was $365 billion.

The chemical sector, which has seen strong growth worldwide, now accounts for roughly 10 per cent of total trade in all goods, according to the U.N. Economic Commission for Europe's (ECE) annual bulletin of trade in chemical products.
By 1995 it had doubled in value since 1989, when trade in chemicals and chemical products amounted to $230 billion.
Western Europe accounted for more than half of world imports in chemicals ($249 billion) in 1995 and nearly two-thirds of world exports ($279 billion), according to the latest report.
"Chemical trade contributes some $30 billion to the western European trade balance, which is a substantial amount of cash," ECE analyst Howard Hornfeld, who wrote the study, told Reuters.
"Chemical trade generates a $46 billion trade deficit in Asia, which imports some $116 billion," he added.
The United States imported $42.2 billion in 1995 while exporting some $60.8 billion worth.
The 470-page document gives detailed import and export trade data for 85 chemicals and chemical products in value terms.

Data are based on statistics reported to the Geneva-based agency by the leading 22 producing and consuming countries. It excludes the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) whose countries do not report to the ECE.
